title: A 660-tonne steel ball hangs inside Taipei 101 to calm its sway
body: Tall buildings sway in strong winds and earthquakes. Near the top of Taipei 101, a steel sphere weighing about 660 tonnes hangs from cables as a tuned mass damper. When the tower moves one way, the heavy pendulum lags behind and pulls against the motion, while hydraulic dampers turn its swinging into heat. This reduces the sway people feel, and the giant ball has become a tourist attraction itself.
